transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess what brings me in is... I got pretty worked up in a staff meeting recently. I started acting out this whole fall-prevention drill right there in the room. I was moving chairs around and waving my arms everywhere, and... I just couldn't seem to stop doing it, even when folks told me to sit down.
Did anyone in the meeting seem to understand what you were trying to do with the fall-prevention drill?

No, not really. They just looked at me like I was crazy. A couple of them told me to sit down and be quiet, but... I don't think anyone actually got what I was trying to show them. They just seemed confused and maybe a little annoyed.
Did you feel like your thoughts were connected and made sense to you during that staff meeting?

I mean... yeah, to me they did. I wasn't confused about what I was doing. I was just trying to show them how to keep people from falling, and it felt like it made perfect sense at the time. I just... I guess my mind was going a mile a minute, but the thoughts themselves seemed fine to me.
Did you have any other thoughts or ideas during that meeting that seemed unrelated to the fall-prevention drill?

Yeah, it wasn't just the drill. My mind just jumps around a lot. Like, it'll go from thinking about my job, to church, to my wife, and then to these new ideas I have for a workshop. It all just happens so fast. Honestly, I end up losing the first thought before I can even get the words out right.
Do you often find it hard to keep track of what you're saying or thinking because your thoughts are disjointed?

No, not really. I mean, my thoughts are fast, like I said, and they bounce around a lot, but they don't feel disjointed to me. It's more like I just have too many of them at once, not that they don't make sense or connect in my head. I know what I'm trying to say, it's just hard to get it all out before the next thought takes over.
Did you ever think that your ideas about the fall-prevention drill or any of your other thoughts were unrealistic or strange?

No, I didn't think they were strange at all. I mean, they felt completely real and important to me at the time. I was just trying to do my job and share my ideas. It didn't cross my mind that anyone else would see it as unrealistic.
Have you ever believed something to be true that others did not believe, and you were certain it was true despite what they said?

Yeah. I mean, even when I'm completely calm and just having a regular day, I'm still sure that my supervisor and a couple of people at work are keeping notes on me. They test me, just through these little comments they make. I know they're trying to build a case or prove that I'm not safe to be around the seniors I take care of. Other people might not see it, but I know it's happening.
Do you think these people at work are trying to harm you or is it more about them trying to prove something about you?

I don't think they want to physically hurt me. Like I was just saying, it's definitely about them trying to prove something. Even on a normal day when I'm totally calm, I just know they're watching me and keeping those notes. They drop those little comments just to test me, because they want to build a case to show I'm not safe around the seniors. So yeah, it's about proving I shouldn't be working there, not about actually harming me.
Do you often find yourself having trouble expressing your thoughts in a way that others can understand?

No, not really. I mean, I think I explain things fine. People might not always agree with me, like with the notes they're taking, but they understand what I'm saying. I don't get mixed up or have trouble getting my point across.
Do you feel like your thoughts are organized and logical to you most of the time?

Yeah, I'd say so. I mean... my thoughts make perfectly good sense to me. They're organized just fine. I don't feel like my brain is all over the place or anything like that. Everything I'm thinking is pretty logical, at least to me.
Do you think the people at work who are keeping notes on you are doing it because they have a personal vendetta against you?

I wouldn't really call it a personal vendetta. I mean, I don't think they just hate me for no reason. It's mostly my supervisor and a couple of other people there. Like I was saying, even when I'm completely calm and just doing my job, I'm still sure they're keeping those notes on me and testing me with those little comments. It's just that they're trying to prove I'm not safe to be around the seniors. That's what it's all about, not really a personal grudge.
Do you think the people at work are plotting against you specifically?

Yeah, I guess you could call it plotting. I mean, like I was just saying, it is aimed at me specifically. Even on days when I'm completely calm and just doing my job, I'm sure my supervisor and those couple of coworkers are keeping those notes on me. They keep testing me with those little comments. They're just trying to build a case to prove I'm not safe to be around the seniors. So, yeah, it's definitely directed at me.
Do you think the people at work who are keeping notes on you want to cause you harm in any way?

I don't think they want to physically hurt me, no. It's really just what I was saying a minute ago. Even when I'm completely calm and just doing my work, I'm sure my supervisor and those couple of people are keeping notes on me and testing me with those little comments. The harm they want to do is just to my job. They're trying to prove I'm not safe around the seniors, probably so they can get rid of me. But no, I don't think they want to physically harm me.
Do you often feel like your thoughts are racing and you can't control them?

Yeah, I do. It happens a lot. My mind just... it jumps around. Like, I'll be thinking about my job, and then it jumps to church, and then to my wife, or to these new workshop ideas I have. It all goes so fast that I end up losing the first thought before I can even say it right. I just can't keep hold of them.
Do you think your thoughts are disorganized when you're not in a situation like the staff meeting?

Well, yeah, sometimes they are. But I guess what really brings me in here is what happened at work, at that staff meeting. I just... I got really worked up. I started acting out this whole fall-prevention drill, moving chairs around, waving my arms everywhere to show them how to do it. And I just couldn't seem to stop, even when people were telling me to sit down and be quiet. My thoughts were just moving too fast, and my body was just going with them.
Do you think the people at work are trying to harm your reputation on purpose?

Yeah, I do think it's on purpose. Like I was saying a few minutes ago... even when I'm just perfectly calm and minding my own business, I'm sure my supervisor and those couple of coworkers are keeping notes on me. They keep testing me with those little comments. So yeah, I think they're doing it on purpose to make me look bad, just to try and prove I'm not safe around the seniors.
Do you still believe that your supervisor and coworkers are keeping notes on you and testing you?

Yeah, I do. Like I just said, even when I'm completely calm, I'm still sure of it. My supervisor and a couple of the people at work are definitely keeping notes on me. And they keep testing me with those little comments. They're just trying to prove that I'm not safe around the seniors.
Have you ever stopped believing that your supervisor and coworkers are keeping notes on you and testing you?

No, I haven't. It doesn't matter if I'm having a good day or if I'm completely calm, I still know it's happening. I'm sure my supervisor and those couple of coworkers are keeping notes on me. They're always testing me with those little comments they make. It never really stops... they're just constantly trying to prove I'm not safe to be around the seniors.
Have your beliefs about people at work keeping notes on you ever changed over time?

No, they haven't changed. Like I've been saying... even when I'm feeling completely calm, I still feel sure my supervisor and a couple of the people at work are keeping notes on me. They keep testing me with those little comments. It's always the same thing, they're just trying to prove I'm not safe around the seniors.
